<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD only declares variables and defines three functions (`pkgver`, `build`, `package`). Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources the file but does not invoke any of those functions, nor performs any network requests or shell commands. The top‑level section contains no command substitutions, `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or other untrusted invocations. The `source` entry points to a GitHub URL, but that is metadata used later during the build phase; it is not executed while parsing. The `sha256sums` entry is set to `SKIP`, which is a hygiene convention and does not cause a failure of this gate. No code injection or data exfiltration appears in the top‑level scope, so sourcing/parsing the PKGBUILD is benign.
</details>

The .SRCINFO file is a standard, minimal package metadata file for a Git-sourced AUR package. It declares the package name, description, source URL (the project's own upstream GitHub repository), build dependencies (git, go), and a SKIP checksum — which is required and normal for VCS sources. There are no network requests to unrelated hosts, no obfuscated or encoded commands, no file operations outside the package scope, and no use of dangerous utilities like eval or curl in a suspicious context. Everything present is consistent with ordinary Arch Linux packaging practices for a -git package.
</details>
